title: Lemma std(ii) v-resonance: circular renormalization; log-counterterm constant unpinned

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Lemma `lem:std`(ii), "the $v$-resonance" paragraph, eqs. (vres), (commsplit),
(resLL). (Related to in-progress q1-4, but a distinct sub-claim.)

The first resonance, $\mathbf q_N\circ\mathbf C_N-c_{N,2}\mathbf l_N\to(\cdot)$, is now given a
clean order-5/3/1 chaos proof — good. But the second claim, convergence of $\mathbf q_N\circ
v_N$, is argued by inserting the paracontrolled structure (vres), applying the commutator
(commsplit), and reducing to the standard $\mathbf q_N\circ\mathbf l_N-3c_N\mathbf l_N$ (resLL,
with the LINEAR $c_N$). The text then asserts the divergence "is exactly the $c_N$ counterterm
of the remainder equation, which is finite once $v$ is the renormalized remainder."

Two problems:
1. **Circularity.** This is essentially "it converges because the construction of $v$ makes it
   converge." The renormalization of $\mathbf q\circ v$ — in particular whether a $c_{N,2}$-type
   *logarithmic* counterterm is also required here (in addition to the $c_N$ from resLL), and
   with what integer constant — is neither derived nor cited at lemma level.
2. **Load-bearing constant.** The constant multiplying $c_{N,2}$ is exactly what any future
   separation argument (q1-13, the resonance-bracket functional) depends on. It cannot be left
   implicit.

**Fix:** a second-moment chaos computation $\mathbb E\langle \mathbf q_N\circ\mathbf C_N-\lambda
c_{N,2}\mathbf l_N,\varphi\rangle^2$ (and the $v$-analogue) determining the unique $\lambda$ that
removes the $\log N$, thereby (a) proving convergence and (b) pinning the constant.
